AccountsFailure.description: A refusal from the accounts service, any non-2xx: the hub's own failure shape, its words shown as written.

code.description: Sign-in: invalid (400), signin_refused (401: a code or verifier WorkOS refused, or one used before), signin_closed (403), rate_limited (429). Invites: invalid (400: not an email, or no such role), forbidden (403: not an owner's or admin's device, or an admin naming an owner), failed (403: the team is at its limit of people), not_found (404: no such open invite), already_invited (409), already_member (409: the email is a person of the team), invite_refused (409: WorkOS wouldn't send it), not_signed_in_team (409: a team with no sign-in).

AccountsInvite.description: An open invite by email: sent, not yet used, revoked or run out.

AccountsInviteCreateInput.description: POST /accounts/v1/invites on the team's own address, with an owner's or admin's device key: WorkOS emails the person, who joins at their next sign-in with that email. Only an owner names an owner.

AccountsInviteCreateOutput.description: 200: the invite made; WorkOS has sent the email.

AccountsInviteListOutput.description: GET /accounts/v1/invites, with an owner's or admin's device key: the team's open invites by email, newest first.

AccountsInviteRevokeOutput.description: POST /accounts/v1/invites/{inviteId}/revoke, no body, with an owner's or admin's device key: the invite taken back, here and at WorkOS.

AccountsSignInInput.description: POST /v1/app/sign-in: what WorkOS sent the browser back with, and this device's name. The service redeems the code with WorkOS itself and keeps no token it got; no auth header.

code.description: WorkOS's authorization code, from the redirect.

codeVerifier.description: The PKCE verifier (RFC 7636) whose S256 challenge the authorize URL carried.

deviceName.description: Names the key each team's /pair makes: the computer's or phone's name.

redirectUri.description: Exactly the redirect_uri the authorize URL carried: a loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/signin/callback` or `fleetd://signin/callback`.

AccountsSignInOutput.description: 200: who signed in and every team they are in, each with a pairing code for its /pair. A first sign-in makes the person's team in the same call.

sessionId.description: WorkOS's session id, which sign-out ends. The app keeps it and the email, nothing else of WorkOS.

id.description: The team's id in the service.

pairingCode.description: A pairing code (`ABCD-2345`) for this person on this team: one use, 15 minutes.

url.description: The team's hub address, an https origin with no path (http only on 127.0.0.1, for tests).

HubRole.description:
What a person may do on the hub. Owners and admins invite people, change roles and change hub-wide settings;
members work in projects. Each device is still capped by its own grants.

description: fleetd cloud's accounts service: the one call an app makes to sign in (and the one to sign out), and a team's invites by email on its own address. Each definition is one body: compile `Accounts.json#/$defs/<Name>`.
